# A customer and a vendor carrying a key this tool has no setter for.
#
# Anything the format does not know is kept in a slot beside the object and
# written back out on export, so a ledger can carry a field this tool does not
# understand and not lose it.
#
# Dropping such a key from the ledger has to take it off the object too — and
# that is the case the writer skipped: it wrote the slot only when the file
# still had something to put in it, so the last key could never be removed.
# The object then differed from the file for good, and every import from then
# on reported `updated` and saved the book again.
#
# The same skip is what a book written before vendors had addresses runs into:
# its vendor's address sits in this slot, the new code sets the real address
# and leaves the slot, and the export then writes every address line twice.
#
# an_owner_after_dropping_a_custom_key.txt is this file without the key.
#
# What this fixture produces: two owners carrying `department`.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_dropping_a_custom_key_takes_it_off.py.
2026-01-01 commodity CAD
	mnemonic: "CAD"
	fullname: "Canadian Dollar"
	namespace: "CURRENCY"
	fraction: 100

customer "C-KEY"
	name: "Acme Supplies"
	currency: CAD
	department: "north"

vendor "V-KEY"
	name: "Beta Printing"
	currency: CAD
	department: "south"

2026-01-01 open Income
	type: Income
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Income:Sales
	type: Income
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"

invoice "INV-KEY"
	customer_id: "C-KEY"
	currency: CAD
	date_opened: 2026-01-01
	department: "north"
	entry:
		date: 2026-01-01
		description: "A line"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
